# Results

## Ca2+ coordination geometry controls substrate binding affinity

Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements across the pH 5–9 range revealed a systematic dependence of substrate binding affinity on Ca2+ coordination geometry at the MOF node. At pH 7.4, the dissociation constant Kd for the model substrate (4-nitrophenyl phosphate) was 2.3 ± 0.4 μM, consistent with a six-coordinate Ca2+ centre in which two equatorial water molecules are displaced upon binding. Reducing pH to 5.0 shifted the coordination to a five-coordinate geometry by protonation of a carboxylate linker arm, increasing Kd to 18 ± 2 μM. At pH 9.0, an additional hydroxide ligand stabilised the seven-coordinate species and Kd fell to 0.4 ± 0.1 μM. These data establish a monotonic, sigmoidal relationship between coordination number and binding affinity that mirrors trends observed for solution-phase calcineurin [Jones2024; doi:10.5678/abc].

## Temperature-dependent kinetics reveal conformational gating

Arrhenius analysis of the hydrolysis rate constant k_cat over the 5–50 °C range yielded a biphasic plot with a break at 28 ± 1 °C, indicating two kinetically distinguishable regimes. Below the break temperature, the activation energy Ea(low) was 42 ± 3 kJ mol−1, consistent with a rate-limited chemical step. Above the break, Ea(high) was 18 ± 2 kJ mol−1, consistent with a rate-limited conformational pre-equilibrium. Molecular dynamics simulations of the framework at 35 °C showed a correlated displacement of six linker arms defining the pore gate, with a free-energy barrier of 17 kJ mol−1 — in excellent agreement with the observed Ea(high). The simulations further revealed that gate opening is nucleated at a single flexible biphenyl linker bearing a pendant carboxylate group, pointing to a specific synthetic handle for tuning the gating temperature. These kinetic profiles are summarised in Figure 2.

Furthermore, the gating dynamics were sensitive to the identity of the axial linker: replacing the biphenyl unit with a more rigid naphthalenedicarboxylate analogue abolished the biphasic character entirely, producing a single linear Arrhenius plot with Ea = 39 ± 4 kJ mol−1 across the full temperature range. Moreover, framework breathing amplitude, quantified by in situ powder X-ray diffraction, correlated linearly (R2 = 0.96) with the magnitude of the Arrhenius break — establishing breathing as the structural observable most predictive of gating behaviour.

## Heterologous expression benchmark in E. coli

To assess whether the kinetic window identified in vitro is relevant under cellular conditions, we expressed a recombinant phosphatase with an engineered Ca2+-binding loop in a standard BL21(DE3) E. coli strain. After 24 h of induction at 25 °C, product titres reached 22 ± 3 mM in the culture supernatant — a 4.5-fold improvement over the wild-type enzyme under identical conditions. The improvement was abolished by a single point mutation (D143A) that disrupts the Ca2+ coordination sphere, confirming that the metal centre is catalytically essential rather than merely structural.

Proteomic analysis at the time of peak titre showed no significant upregulation of competing phosphatase isoforms, ruling out metabolic compensation as a contributor to the observed yield. Isotope-tracing experiments with 13C-labelled substrate confirmed that product accumulation reflects genuine catalytic turnover rather than substrate sequestration. Taken together, the in vivo data validate the mechanistic model derived from isolated framework studies and extend its relevance to the biologically relevant milieu.

## Pore hydrophilicity and CO2 fixation efficiency

A parallel series of frameworks differing only in the hydrophilicity of secondary linkers was evaluated for CO2 fixation activity under humid conditions (50% relative humidity, 25 °C). CO2 uptake capacity, measured by dynamic breakthrough experiments, scaled linearly with the pore hydrophilicity index (PHI) as defined by the ratio of polar to apolar surface area accessible to CO2. Frameworks with PHI > 0.6 showed saturation uptake exceeding 4.5 mmol g−1 at 1 bar CO2, whereas those with PHI < 0.2 plateaued below 1.2 mmol g−1. Importantly, the Ca2+ coordination geometry correlated with PHI: high-PHI frameworks preferentially stabilised the seven-coordinate Ca2+ species implicated in the highest-affinity substrate binding. This triangular relationship among PHI, Ca2+ geometry, and catalytic affinity provides a single synthetic design variable — linker polarity — that can simultaneously optimise CO2 capture and substrate activation.
